claim: Pure Malbolge stored-program control flow for five fixed 11-byte shapes. The opcode and the bytes that are emitted are loaded from RAM. JMP (0x0C) emits prog_6. JZ (opcode 0x01, condition in prog_1) emits prog_8 when the condition is 0 and prog_7 when it is 1. CALL (0x0E) emits prog_8 and then prog_4. Same binary, both engines, matching step counts, under the 59049 limit.
scope: These five shapes only. The JMP immediate is read from RAM; the jump target is not a selector, so landing on HALT is not demonstrated. JZ distinguishes only condition 0 from condition 1. CALL is one frame deep. Not a general program counter and not arbitrary MBIR.

cases.name: JMP skip HALT
cases.description: Opcode 0x0C emits prog_6 (0x41). The target byte is not classified.

cases.name: JMP other immediate
cases.description: Same path with prog_6 = 0x58, so the emitted byte is the one loaded from RAM.

cases.name: CALL then return byte
cases.description: Opcode 0x0E emits prog_8 (0x42) and then prog_4 (0x41).

not_demonstrated: A general program counter that fetches arbitrary MBIR.
Using the JMP target as a selector. Landing on HALT is not in this image.
JZ for any condition other than 0 versus 1.
A call stack deeper than one frame.
The 14 streaming ALU vectors and CMP_EQ in this image.
